chunks.title: Early Experience Paradigm Overview
chunks.summary: High-level overview of the Early Experience (EE) paradigm, showing how it bridges imitation learning (IL) and reinforcement-learning-like (RL-like) interaction via a closed loop: data construction → dual-method training (IWM + SR) → policy update → looped data reconstruction, yielding policy π_EE.

chunks.title: Expert Data and Initial Policy Interaction
chunks.summary: Main pipeline starting point: defines the expert dataset D_expert, the initial LLM policy π_0, and how non-expert actions are sampled for given expert states and executed in the environment to obtain future states for both expert and non-expert actions.

chunks.title: Reward-Free Rollout Data Construction
chunks.summary: Constructs the reward-free rollout dataset D_rollout from environment interactions, organizing triplets (s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j) as early experience data without using environment rewards.

chunks.title: Dual-Method Training Fork from D_rollout
chunks.summary: A branching entry node that takes D_rollout and conceptually splits it into two parallel training paths: IWM (Implicit World Modeling) and SR (Self-Reflection), which share input but have different objectives and outputs.

chunks.title: IWM: Implicit World Modeling Branch
chunks.summary: The IWM branch uses rollout data to train the policy model as an implicit world model. It predicts future states s_i^j from (s_i, a_i^j) via a next-token prediction objective, producing gradients that internalize environment dynamics into the policy parameters.

chunks.title: SR: Self-Reflection Branch and Reflection Data
chunks.summary: The SR branch compares expert and non-expert outcomes, generates natural language explanations c_i^j of why expert actions are better, constructs a reflection dataset D_refl, and jointly trains the policy to imitate expert actions and produce explanations.

chunks.title: Policy Update and Early Experience Loop
chunks.summary: Merges training signals from IWM and SR to update the policy into π_EE, which encodes both world dynamics and expert behavior with explanations. The updated policy is fed back to the data-construction stage to generate new early experience, forming a closed loop without using rewards.

chunks.title: IL and RL-like Conceptual Bridging
chunks.summary: Conceptual background annotations that group parts of the diagram into imitation learning (IL) and reinforcement-learning-like interaction (RL-like), and highlight that the EE paradigm bridges IL and RL via early, reward-free experience.

nodes.desc: Main title text: "Early Experience (EE) Paradigm: Bridging IL and RL".

Short description explaining that EE is an early experience paradigm based on expert demonstrations and environment interactions, constructing reward-free rollout data and jointly training world modeling and self-reflection to obtain policy π_EE.
Simplified pipeline element labeled "Expert Data / D_expert" as the starting point in the high-level overview.
Simplified pipeline element labeled "EE Training (IWM + SR)" representing the dual-method training stage in the overview.
Simplified pipeline element labeled "Policy π_EE & Loop Back" indicating the resulting EE policy and its feedback into the loop at the overview level.

Module box labeled "Expert Dataset D_expert" containing the definition D_expert = {(s_i, a_i)} and explaining that s_i are expert states and a_i are corresponding expert actions, possibly shown as a small table of (s, a) pairs.
Formula or text annotation inside or near the expert dataset clarifying D_expert = {(s_i, a_i)}.
Module box labeled "Initial Policy π_0 (LLM)" or "Initial LLM Policy", indicating the language-model-based policy used to sample non-expert actions.
Text annotation showing action sampling: for each state s_i from D_expert, sample K non-expert actions {a_i^1, ..., a_i^K} ~ π_0(·|s_i).
Shape representing the set of sampled non-expert actions {a_i^1, ..., a_i^K} associated with a given state s_i.
Module box labeled "Environment" representing the environment in which state-action pairs are executed to obtain next states.

Annotation describing environment transitions: executing expert pair (s_i, a_i) yields expert next state s_{i+1}, while executing non-expert pairs (s_i, a_i^j) yields alternative outcomes s_i^j, marked as counterfactual or alternative outcomes.
Module box labeled "Rollout Data (No Reward)" or "Early Experience Data Construction" representing the dataset D_rollout constructed from environment interactions.
Text specifying D_rollout = { (s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j) } and emphasizing that rewards are not included; only state transitions for both expert and non-expert actions are stored.
Annotation highlighting that D_rollout is reward-free, based on early policy rollouts, and may be shown as a simple table of multiple (s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j) triplets.
Small branching node labeled "Dual Training on D_rollout" acting as a fork that splits the rollout data into two parallel paths.
Annotation or arrow label indicating branch toward "IWM: Implicit World Modeling" from the dual training node.
Annotation or arrow label indicating branch toward "SR: Self-Reflection" from the dual training node.
Module box titled "IWM: Implicit World Modeling" representing the IWM training branch operating on rollout data.
Input description for IWM: uses (s_i, a_i^j) from D_rollout as conditions and aims to predict future state s_i^j.
Loss formulation or explanation such as L_IWM = -log p_θ(s_i^j | s_i, a_i^j), interpreted as a next-token prediction or language modeling loss over tokens describing the future state.
Annotation indicating that the IWM loss provides a "World Dynamics Internalization" or "Environment Model Signal" gradient that updates the shared policy parameters θ.
Module box titled "SR: Self-Reflection" representing the self-reflection training branch.
Small comparison module illustrating the contrast between expert outcome s_{i+1} and non-expert outcome s_i^j (e.g., two side-by-side boxes labeled s_{i+1} and s_i^j with a "compare outcomes" label).
LLM explanation-generation module that takes the comparison of s_{i+1} vs. s_i^j (plus state s_i and actions) and outputs explanations c_i^j.
Text describing c_i^j as explanations of why expert action a_i is better than non-expert action a_i^j.
Module box labeled "Reflection Data D_refl" containing training samples of the form (s_i, a_i, c_i^j) or similar, representing state, expert action, and explanation triplets.
Module box labeled "Policy + Explainer Training" or similar, representing supervised training of the policy (and explanation head) using D_expert and D_refl.
Annotation describing the SR loss as a combination of action supervision and explanation supervision, e.g., L_SR = L_action + L_explanation.
Module box titled "Policy Update & Early Experience Loop" representing the aggregation of IWM and SR training signals to update the policy.
Small merge node or annotation indicating that gradients or losses from IWM and SR are combined here to form a joint optimization objective.
Module box labeled "π_EE (Updated Policy)" representing the resulting Early Experience policy that integrates world dynamics understanding and expert imitation with explanations.

Curved or loop arrow annotation describing that π_EE is fed back to replace π_0 in the data construction stage to generate new early experience without environment rewards, enabling multiple iterations of the loop.
Background or side label "Imitation Learning (IL)" associated with D_expert, D_refl, and the supervised policy + explanation training components.
Background or side label "Reinforcement Learning-like Interaction (RL-like)" associated with environment rollouts, D_rollout, and the IWM branch, emphasizing interaction without explicit rewards.
Conceptual annotation such as "EE bridges IL and RL via early, reward-free experience" placed between or overlapping the IL and RL-like regions.
